description.cancellation_policy:
Reservations cannot be sold or transferred to other people. Only the group leader or listed alternate can pick up or use the permit. Leader or alternate leader names cannot be changed or added.

Changes you can make online:

  • Changes to group size can be made if quota space is available. 
  • Change of entry trail, entry date, or permit type requires a new reservation for the desired trip. You will pay new reservation and recreation fees. 
  • Cancel your reservation online, the per person recreation fee will be refunded automatically if you complete the cancelation at least 12 days before entry date.
  • Corrections to itinerary, exit date or exit location can be done online or when the permit is issued.

Refunds:

No refund of the $6 reservation fee. A refund of the per person fee will be granted 12 days in advance of a trip. Log onto your account at Recreation.gov to make changes or call Sierra National Forest for reservation assistance, (559) 855-5355.
description.description:
Located in California's beautiful Sierra Nevada Mountains, Sierra National Forest offers challenging trails, high mountain peaks and unparalleled views. Several of our trails give entry to the John Muir Trail or Pacific Crest Trail with the opportunity to trek in the longest roadless section of the Sierra Nevada Mountain Range. Our trails offer possibilities for hiking, photography, peak bagging, fishing, or simply enjoying the pristine beauty of the High Sierra. Whether you are seeking solitude, exceptional scenery, or sharing a wilderness adventure, there are many ways to create a memorable experience.

Come, take a deep breath of clean mountain air. Put on your pack and hit the trail. Come to experience nature and let it refresh your spirit. Places to explore include the Ansel Adams, John Muir, Dinkey Lakes, and Kaiser wildernesses. Trips beginning on Sierra National Forest may continue into the wilderness areas of Yosemite, Sequoia, and Kings Canyon National Parks or Inyo National Forest. 

As you plan your trip, remember that we must take care of this amazing place. While you are here, be respectful of water, woods and wildlife. Travel lightly on the land. Remember to leave this place undamaged so it will continue to be what we seek of wilderness.
description.discounts:
There are no discounts or permit exemptions for age, military service, civil service, students, or persons with disabilities. 

National Interagency Passes are not accepted for wilderness permits.
description.driving_directions:
Directions to each trail can be found on the Sierra National Forest webpage under hiking and the trail name. 

High Sierra Ranger District Office is located in Prather, CA, immediately after the roundabout on the right-hand side of the road as you continue up towards the mountains. The address is 29688 Auberry Road Prather CA 93651

Bass Lake Ranger District Office is located in North Fork, CA, approximately 17 miles east of Highway 41. The office is in the center of town on the left when coming from Highway 41. The address is 57003 Road 225 North Fork CA 93643
description.fee_policy:
Reservation Fee:

A $6.00 non-refundable reservation fee is required for each permit reservation. 

Recreation Fee:

A per person recreation fee is charged for your group when reserving a wilderness permit for entry on Sierra National Forest trails. 

The recreation fees are used to finance the on-the-ground wilderness programs in Sierra National Forest. 

  • A $5.00 per person recreation fee is charged for all areas aside from those permits exiting at Mt. Whitney.
  • Permits exiting Mt Whitney must select that option in the drop down and the fee is $15 per person.

There are no discounts for annual passes, military, seniors, or children. All people count for wilderness quotas and fees.

Fees cannot be transferred to other dates or trails. No rain checks or credits.
description.need_to_know_email:
Your reservation will be canceled as a no show unless you pick up the permit on your scheduled depart date or arrange for late pick up before the entry date. Link to Permit Pick up Instructions. 

Permit Pick Up

You must call the office where you will be picking up your permit, 3 days before your start date, to confirm your reservation and have your permit printed. 

  • Permits are issued 1 to 2 days before the entry date or on the entry date.

  • Group leader or alternate should bring photo identification and reservation number when requesting the permit. 

  • Review the leader responsibility and permit policy in Permit Pick up Instructions. 

Changes, Cancellations, Refunds

  • Changes to group size can be made if space is available.

  • Change of entry trail, entry date, or permit type requires a new reservation. All fees apply.

  • Cancel your reservation 12 days before entry date for per person recreation fee refund.

  • Corrections to itinerary, exit date or exit location can be done online or when the permit is issued.

  • No refund if you cancel your reservation 12 days or less before the entry date. No refund of reservation fee.

Risk & Responsibility

  • Come prepared to find your way. Most of the area has no cell service. 

  • Check weather and trail conditions. 

  • Download maps and emergency information before your trip.

  • Bring adequate supplies of food, water and clothing.

  • Learn symptoms of altitude sickness.

Be Bear Aware!

  • Do not leave food or refuse car or tent. 

  • Do not leave food unattended. 

  • Secure food and trash in bear resistant food storage containers.

General Regulations

  • Do not feed wildlife. 

  •  Campfires are subject to current fire restrictions.

  • Pack-out all trash, food and gear. Do not burn or bury food or trash. 

  • No drones, they are prohibited in wilderness.

  • Do not camp on vegetation, move rocks, build walls, or disturb soils to “improve” a camp site. 

  • No pets allowed in National Parks. 

Learn more about Wilderness regulations in the Sierra National Forest.
description.need_to_know_order:
No Show

Your reservation will be canceled as a no show after your arrival date, unless you pick up the permit or arrange for a late night box pick up . Permit Pick up Instructions. 

Wilderness Permit

The group leader is responsible for picking up the permit and relaying wilderness information to your group. You are accepting responsibility as leader that your group will follow all of the rules and regulations, including:   

  • Signed permit must be in the group leader’s possession; show to trail rangers upon request. 
  • Everyone in the group must start on entry date and location stated in the permit. 
  • The permit expires after the exit date stated in the permit. 
  • Permits will not be issued with a stay period greater than 14 days in one area. 
  • A permit is valid for continuous wilderness travel, including across the boundary of adjacent wilderness areas in our neighboring parks or forests. However, leaving the trail to enter at a different location requires a new permit.

Group Size

  • You cannot exceed the group size stated in the permit.
  • Groups cannot combine if they would exceed 15 people.
  • People of all ages count for group size, quotas and fees. 

Reservation Policy

  • Only the group leader or alternate listed on the original reservation can pick up or use the permit. Show photo ID when requested. 
  • Reservation or permit cannot be sold or transferred. Alternate leaders cannot be changed or added. 
  • A reservation receipt or confirmation letter is not accepted as proof of a valid permit or reservation. 
  • There are no discounts for wilderness permits. 
  • Fees are not transferable, no rain check or credit.

Risk and Responsibility

  • Come prepared to find your way. Do not rely on cell phone for communication or navigation, most of the area has no cell service. 
  • Check weather and trail conditions. 
  • Plan to be self-sufficient, bring adequate food, water and clothing.
  • Learn symptoms of altitude sickness.
description.need_to_know_permit:
Permit Pickup Instructions

  • Please call the Sierra National Forest up to three days before the trip at either the Prather office: 559-855-5355 or North Fork Office: 559-877-2210. You can verify the pick up day and time when you call the issuing office. If you plan on picking up your permit before or after operating hours of the station, let them know at that time.

  •  No shows are processed after your arrival date. Reserved permits can be picked up one or two days before the entry date, or on the entry date.

The signed permit must be in the group leader’s possession during the trip and must be presented to rangers upon request. The group leader signing the permit is accepting responsibility to ensure everyone in their group will follow the rules and regulations on the permit. Wilderness regulations are enforceable with maximum penalties of $5,000 and/or 6 months in jail. 

Be Bear Aware!

  • Do not leave food or refuse in your car or tent. Do not leave food unattended. 

  • In campgrounds and parking areas with bear proof lockers, all food and scented items must be removed from vehicles and secured in the lockers. Dispose of trash in bear resistant trash cans. 

  • Bear resistant food storage containers are recommended for all wilderness travelers. Review wilderness rules for specific areas where containers are required.

Human Waste Disposal

Solid human waste should be buried six to eight inches deep and at least 100 feet or more from water sources, trails, or campsites.

Behave Responsibly

Respect other visitor’s desire for quiet and solitude. Please help protect this natural resource and leave it unmarked for future visitors. Familiarize yourself with the seven principles of Leave No Trace and review wilderness rules: 

  • Pack out all your trash.

  • Protect water quality, don’t use soap in natural waterways, even biodegradable soap can damage aquatic life. Waste water should be scattered at least 100 feet away from any water source.

  • Don’t cut switchbacks; shortcutting damages the trail and adds to erosion.

  • No drones; they are prohibited in wilderness.

  • No loud audio devices; let the sounds of nature be part of the wilderness experience.

  • Campfires are restricted in many areas; wood growth is very slow at high elevation and what little wood exists helps sustain the natural soil, plant and animal community.

  • Do not camp on vegetation, these fragile areas are easily damaged. Choose a campsite at least 100 feet away from lakes, streams, or trails.

Risk & Responsibility

  • Come prepared to find your way. Most of the forest has no cell service. 

  • Check weather and trail conditions. 

  • Download maps, and emergency information before starting on the trail.

  • Plan to be self-sufficient, bring adequate supplies of food, water and clothing.

  • Learn symptoms of altitude sickness.

Wilderness Backcountry

Activities like backpacking, hiking, skiing, and mountaineering and horse camping are allowed. Motorized or mechanical activities like mountain biking or drones are not allowed in wilderness. There are maintained trails through the area to hike on, but no developed campground facilities. Once you start on the trail, there are no water faucets and no restrooms.   

Crossing Park & Forest Boundaries

One permit is valid for continuous wilderness travel, including traveling through adjacent parks and forests. Provide the exit location, exit date and itinerary information to indicate your full travel plan. 

You must follow the local rules while you are in each park or forest. Check regulations for each area you will visit regarding pets, food storage, camping and campfire restrictions, stay limits, smaller group size limits for off trail routes. No pets in National Parks. 

Trips ending at Mt Whitney (Whitney Portal- Inyo National Forest) must be identified in your Sierra NF permit.
description.no_show_policy:
Your reservation will be canceled as a No Show and your space may go to other groups, unless you pick up your permit or arrange for a late drop box pick up.

  • Call the Sierra National Forest up to three days before the trip at either the Prather office: (559) 855-5355 or North Fork office: (559) 877-2218 to verify your final group size and pick up time and date. You can also arrange for after hours drop box pick up at that time.

Reserved permits can be picked up one or two days before the entry date, or on the entry date at the selected pick up location.
description.quota_details:
Permits are required year round.

The number of people allowed to begin overnight trips is limited by year-round quotas. 

When selecting quota, you are reserving a specific start date and entry trail. You only need space on the entry date. 

List of Trail Names and Quota 

  • If part of your group will enter on a different date or trail to meet you in the backcountry, they must have their own permit and fit into the quota.

  • Off trail travel is limited by quota; wilderness permit office can help identify quota needed.

  • No trail exit quota applies on the Sierra.

Group size limits ensure people spread out to prevent impacts.

  • All ages count for group size/quotas.

  • Max group size is 15 people. Yosemite, Sequoia, and Kings Canyon National Parks have group size limits of 8-12 in some areas.

  • Walk-up Quota is only available on line at recreation.gov, 14 days in advance of an arrival date. We do not create walk-up permits at the Stations.

Groups on separate permits cannot combine if they exceed max group.
description.season_information:
A permit is required year-round for overnight trips into John Muir, Ansel Adams, Dinkey Lakes and Kaiser Wildernesses, and Inyo National Forest, as well Sequoia, Kings Canyon, and Yosemite National Parks. Only the leader or alternate specified in the reservation may pick up or use the permit. 

Each year quota season permits become available for advanced reservations six months in advance of your trip start day. 

Permits are released during the first week of January and then 6 months in advance of the start date.

Permit holder accepts responsibility for their group:

  • Signed permit in group leader’s possession.

  • Group must start on entry date and location on permit.

  • You cannot exceed the group size stated on permit and group size cannot exceed 15 people. 

  • Permit is valid for continuous wilderness travel. Exiting and reentering at a different location voids permit. 

  • Permit expires after exit date.

Trips sponsored by organizations or commercial groups must call 559-855-5355 for permits.

44585801.description:
The Onion Springs trail is 4.7 miles long. It begins near the High Sierra Pack Station and ends at Four Forks Creek near Wilderness boundary. The trail is open for the following uses: Off Highway Vehicles (OHV), horseback riding, mountain biking, hiking, and backpacking for those without high clearance vehicles headed to Margaret Lakes Basin.

Common Destinations: Arch Rock, Frog Lake, Margaret Lakes Basin, Heitz Meadow, Rattlesnake Lake, and Cassidy Crossing.

Onion Springs OHV/Margaret Lakes Trail Map

Onion Springs Trail Area:

  • No campfires above 10,000 ft.
  • There are site specific campfire restrictions in some of these areas. 
  • Food and refuse must be stored in a container designed to prevent access by bears, or counter-balanced at least 15 feet above the ground and 10 feet horizontally from a tree trunk (where containers are not required).
  • Ansel Adams Wilderness regulations apply.

44585801.name: Onion Springs OHV/Margaret Lakes

44585802.description:
The Mono Meadow trail is 4.3 miles long which spans from Lake Tomas Edison to Mono Hot Springs Resort. Mono Meadow Trail intersects two other faint trails that heads Northwest towards Warm Creek Trail, as well as the Tule Lake Trail and Doris Lake Trail. 

Common Destinations: Mono Creek, Tule Lake, Doris Lake, and Mono Hot Springs.

44585803.description:
The Doris/Tule Trail is a 3.1 mile out and back trail that begins at Mono Hot Springs Resort. The trail leads to Doris and Tule Lakes, Mono Meadow Trail, and a few faint connecter trails which intersect with Warm Creek Trail. It is a popular trail due to the proximity of Mono Hot Springs Resort and receives a fair amount of use; popular with day hikers, fishermen and backpackers looking for a short hike or an overnight adventure. 

Common Destinations: Doris Lake, Tule Lake, Mono Meadow, Mono Creek, and Devils Table.

44585804.description:
Mono Hot Springs Trail is a 1.9-mile trail connecting to the High Sierra Ranger Station. The popular route to hike is to start at the High Sierra Ranger Station elevation 7400 ft and walk down to the middle fork of the San Joaquin River which is at 6550 feet in elevation. It is a nice trail for short day hikes when the high country is holding snow early season and for fisherman who are looking for solitude on the river down stream of the busy Mono Hot Springs.    

Common Destinations: San Joaquin River, Mono Hot Springs Campground, and High Sierra Ranger Station.

44585805.description:
The Portal Forebay trail is faint foot trail which is about 2 miles down to the San Joaquin River and ties into the Doris and Tule Lake Trail system. Portal Forebay Trail also ties into the Rattlesnake Trail that takes one down to the Portuguese Flat area 3.8 miles, and to the San Juaquin river which is 5.5 miles down to Rattlesnake Crossing. The willing adventurer can find the faint lesser used trail, its 6.2 miles in length where it intersects with a trail leading up to Tule Meadow, and about 9 miles to Heitz Meadow.  

Common Destinations: Mono Crossing on the San Joaquin River, Tule Lake, Portuguese Flat, and Rattlesnake Crossing.

44585806.description:
The Rattlesnake Trail is a faint lesser used trail that drops down from 8100 ft at the trailhead to Portuguese Flat which is 6760 feet in elevation in 3.6 miles. At Portuguese Flat one can take the connecting trail 3.8 miles back to Portal Forebay or descend to Rattlesnake Crossing on the San Joaquin River which is 2 miles below Portuguese Flat. 

Common Destinations: Portuguese Flat, Rattlesnake Crossing, and Mono Crossing.

Logan Meadow Trailhead is located above Mammoth Pool Reservoir by the Wagners Store. The trail is 3.7 miles in length and connects with the French Trail which ends at Piyau Dome Trailhead, 11 miles from the trail junction of China Bar Boat- In.  

Common Destinations: West Fork Creek, Jackass Creek, China Bar, and views of Hell’s Half Acre.

Hells Half Acre trail is a faint trail which is 1.5 miles in length and connects to the French Trail which follows the length of the South fork of the San Joaquin River above Mammoth Pool Reservoir. One can hike 6.7 miles below Arch Rock and Piyau Dome finishing at the Piyau Dome Trailhead, or head south on the French Trail for views of Fuller Buttes and Hells Half Acre.  

Common Destinations: Jackass Rock, Fuller Buttes, Arch Rock, and views of Balloon Dome and the San Juaquin River.

The South Fork trail is 1.8 miles long. It begins at Road 5S69 and connects to the French trail which is 11 miles long and follows the South Fork of the San Juaquin River. The trail goes past Arch Rock and has good views of Piayu Dome, Balloon Dome, and a confluence of the San Juaquin River.  

Common Destinations: French Trail system, Arch Rock, Piyau Dome, and Fuller Buttes.

Piyau Dome Trailhead starts just north of scenic Piyau Dome and ties into the French Trail which in total is 14.7 miles in length ending at Logan Meadow Trailhead. The Piyau Dome Trail is a great accessing point to climb Piayu Dome which is 7811 in elevation and has great views of Balloon Dome and the San Juaquin River canyon.  

Common Destinations: Piyau Dome, French Trail, Granite Creek, and the San Juaquin River.

Important: Trail not currently maintained for stock.

The Cassidy trail is 10.5 miles long. It begins at the end of Road 5S84 and crosses the Middle Fork San Joaquin River at Cassidy Crossing 4.9 miles from the trailhead. After Cassidy Crossing the Cassidy trail climbs quickly up passing Rattlesnake Lake and intersects with Heitz Meadow in 5.6 miles. The Miller Creek trail is 3.5 miles long. It begins at Minarets Pack Station and ends at Cassidy Trailhead 5s84. One can also can also tie in the Miller Creek Trail to the Yellow Jacket Trail which is 2.3 miles in length and ends at Clover Meadow. 

Common Destinations: Cassidy Crossing, Rattlesnake Lake, Heitz Meadow, Cattle Mountain, Miller Creek, and Clover Meadow.

Trail currently not maintained for stock!

The Mammoth trail is 15.8 miles in length, crossing the North Fork of the San Joaquin River at Sheeps Crossing and goes over Granite Stairway pass at 9200 feet in elevation. Then it drops down 5.1 miles through the Inyo National Forest to the Devils Postpile National Monument. The trailhead begins past Clover Meadow Ranger Station at the end of road 5S30. 

Take Beasore Road and turn left on 5S30 (Granite Creek) Rd, to Clover Meadow, stay on this road past Clover Meadow and stay left. After the road crosses Granite Creek turn right. Travel about three more miles to reach the Mammoth Trailhead. There are two bear boxes and a trail head sign on the left of the dirt parking lot.

44585814.description:
The Isberg trail is 11.9 miles long. It begins at Granite Creek Campground 5S33 and ends at Yosemite National Park Boundary at Isberg Pass. 

To get to the trailhead you can either take Beasore Rd or Minarets Rd, either way follow the signs to Clover Meadow. Turn on Rd 5S30 toward Clover Meadow. Go past the Ranger Station and past the turn off to Granite Creek Campground. At the next road junction veer to the right. The trailhead is on your left and parking is available before or after the bridge.

44585815.description:
The Walton trail is 3.2 miles long. It begins at Fernandez Trailhead and ends at Ca Riding & Hiking 24e03. 

Drive 28.5 miles up Beasore Rd and turn left at the Fernandez Trail sign (Rd 5S05). Continue two miles on this dirt road to the large parking area. The Walton Trailhead is in the same parking lot as the Fernandez trailhead.

The Walton trail is to the right, the Fernandez trail to the left. Lillian Lake is 5.9 miles, Rutherford is 8.2 miles from the trailhead. For overnight trips these trailheads have separate quotas. 

The Walton Trail is a great connecting trail to access the Lilian Lake Trail loop, the California Riding and Hiking Trail, the Fernandez Trail, and Post Peak Pass Trail.

44585815.name: Walton

44585816.description:
Drive 28.5 miles up Beasore Rd and turn left at the Fernandez trail sign (Rd 5S05). Continue for two miles on this dirt road to the large parking area. The most common hike from the Fernandez Trailhead is the Lillian Lake Loop which is around 12 miles total. Vanderburgh Lake is 4.25 miles from the trailhead, Lady Lake is 5.25 miles and Lillian Lake is 6.19 miles from the trailhead. 

Common Destinations: Vanderburgh Lake, Lady Lake, Lillian Lake, Staniford Lakes, Chittenden Lake, Flat Lake, Rainbow Lake, and Fernandez Pass.

44585817.description:
The Norris Lake trail is 3.0 miles long. It begins at Norris Trailhead and connects to the Jackass Lakes Trail.

Take Beasore Road to the 5S86 (Norris Lake) road on the left, travel approximately two miles to reach the Norris Trailhead. This trail is a little bit longer than the Jackass Trail but is more of a moderate hike. Stay left on the trail for about two miles to reach Norris Lake (there are no fish in this lake). Another 0.6 miles to Lower Jackass Lake and from there another 0.9 miles to Upper Jackass Lake. This trail can easily be done as a day hike.

The Jackass Lakes trail is 4 miles long. It begins at Beasore Road 5s07 and ends at Upper Jackass Lake.

44585818.description:
The most common destinations from Quartz/Chiquito Trailhead is Chiquito Lake 2.7 miles. Chiquito Trails goes over Chiquito Pass to Yosemite National Park boundary. Chain Lakes is 8.4 miles, and Ottoway Lakes 15.5 miles from the trailhead.

To reach Chiquito Trailhead. take Beasore Rd when you see Globe Rock on the right make a left turn on to road 5S04 (Globe Rock), after about two miles on this road you will reach the trailhead. 

Common destinations for this trailhead are the same as the Quartz Trailhead. There is about 2.7 miles of hiking between the Chiquito and Quartz Trailheads, but the driving time to the Chiquito Trailhead is less.

  • Yosemite wilderness regulations apply if entering the National Park.

44585818.name: Chiquito/Quartz

44585819.description:
The Badger Flat Trailhead is located on Kaiser Pass Road next to the Potter Pass Trailhead. The Badger Flat trail is 3 miles long and intersects with the California Riding and Hiking Trail which continues to Rock Meadow and Coyote Lake. The Badger Flat trail receives less use than the Potter Pass trail which is very popular. The trail eventually becomes a faint user trail which descends to Big Creek at an elevation of 7985 feet.  

Common Destinations: Rancheria Creek, Weldons Camp, Rockhouse Meadow, Rock Meadow, and Coyote Lake. 

Badger Trail Map

description_map.need_to_know:
Badger Flat Area:

  • No campfires above 10,000 ft.
  • Food and refuse must be stored in a container designed to prevent access by bears, or counter-balanced at least 15 feet above the ground and 10 feet horizontally from a tree trunk (where containers are not required).
  • Dinkey Lakes Wilderness regulations apply.

44585819.name: Badger -- This trailhead is for entry into the Dinkey Lakes Wilderness.

44585820.description:
The Helms Meadow trail is 7.8 miles long. It begins at either Courtright Reservoir accessible by boat or at the intersection of the Dusy-Ershim OHV route. The Helms Meadow Trail intersects the Frazier Trail around the lake, The Nelson Lake Trail and eventually connects to Dinkey Lakes Loop and First Dinkey Lake. 

Common Destinations: Helms Creek, Helms Meadow, Nelson Lakes, Cliff Lake, and First Dinkey Lake. 

Helms Meadow Trail Map

description_map.need_to_know:
Helms Meadow Area:

  • No campfires above 10,000 ft.
  • Food and refuse must be stored in a container designed to prevent access by bears, or counter-balanced at least 15 feet above the ground and 10 feet horizontally from a tree trunk (where containers are not required).
  • Dinkey Lakes Wilderness regulations apply.

44585820.name: Helms Meadow

44585821.description:
The Cliff Lake Trail is a popular route which provides access to the Dinkey Lakes Wilderness. The trailhead starts past Trapper Spring campground at an elevation of 8460 feet. In 1.4 miles the trail hits Nelson Creek and the intersection of the Frazier Trail. Cliff lake is a 4.6-mile hike and can be done as a day hike or an overnighter. The hike to Bullfrog lake is 5.4 miles in length, Rock lake is 6.1 miles. Cliff Lake Trail provides access to many of the other trails in Dinkey Lakes Wilderness and Dogtooth Peak.  

Common Destinations: Nelson Creek, Cliff Lake, Nelson Lake, Rock Lake, 2nd Dinkey Lake, and The Dinkey Lakes Loop.

Cliff Lake Trail Map

description_map.need_to_know:
Cliff Lake Area:

  • No campfires above 10,000 ft.
  • Food and refuse must be stored in a container designed to prevent access by bears, or counter-balanced at least 15 feet above the ground and 10 feet horizontally from a tree trunk (where containers are not required).
  • Dinkey Lakes Wilderness regulations apply.

44585821.name: Cliff Lake

44585822.description:
The Nelson Lake trail is 3.7 miles long. It begins at Helms Meadow trail 27e56 (elevation 8440 feet) and ends at Nelson Lake which is 8942 feet in elevation making the total elevation gain of about 500 feet. Nelson Lakes are 5.6 miles from the Cliff Lake trailhead below Nelson Mountain. Trail is open for the following uses: hiking, backpacking, and horseback riding.  

Common Destinations: Nelson Creek, Helms Meadow, Nelson Lakes, Nelson Peak, Brown Peak, and Cliff Lake. 

Nelson Trail Map

description_map.need_to_know:
Nelson Area:

  • No campfires above 10,000 ft.
  • Food and refuse must be stored in a container designed to prevent access by bears, or counter-balanced at least 15 feet above the ground and 10 feet horizontally from a tree trunk (where containers are not required).
  • Dinkey Lakes Wilderness regulations apply.

44585822.name: Nelson

44585823.description:
The Dinkey Lakes Trail provides easy access to the Dinkey Lakes loop and the numerous lakes in Dinkey Lakes Basin. A very popular loop with hikers with many lakes to enjoy in relatively short mileage. Mystery Lake is 2 miles from the trailhead, First Dinkey Lake is 3 miles, Swede Lake is 2.5 miles, and South Lake is 3.2 miles. 

Common destinations: Mystery Lake, First and Second Dinkey Lakes, Rock Lake. Dogtooth Peak, Coyote Lake, and The Three Sisters.

Willow Meadow/Dinkey Lakes Trail Map

Driving Directions to Willow Meadow/Dinkey Lakes Trailhead

description_map.need_to_know:
Willow Meadow/Dinkey Lake Area:

  • No campfires above 10,000 ft.
  • Food and refuse must be stored in a container designed to prevent access by bears, or counter-balanced at least 15 feet above the ground and 10 feet horizontally from a tree trunk (where containers are not required).
  • Dinkey Lakes Wilderness regulations apply.

44585823.name: Willow Meadow/Dinkey Lake

44585824.description:
This shared OHV route is 2.2 miles long and features Coyote Lake which can be accessed by the Coyote OHV Route, by Willow Meadow/ Dinkey Lakes Trailhead 5.4 miles, and Badger Flat TH which is 7.6 miles one way. Coyote Lake is a unique lake for three sides of the lake is in the Dinkey Wilderness and one side is open for OHV use with jeeps or trucks with high clearance, providing access to multiple types of recreation user groups. A beautiful lake at 9004 feet in elevation. 

Common Destinations: Coyote Lake, Red Lake, Perkins Camp, Rock Meadow, First Dinkey Lake, and Black Peak.  

Coyote Lake Trail Map

description_map.need_to_know:
Coyote Area:

  • No campfires above 10,000 ft.
  • Food and refuse must be stored in a container designed to prevent access by bears, or counter-balanced at least 15 feet above the ground and 10 feet horizontally from a tree trunk (where containers are not required).
  • Dinkey Lakes Wilderness regulations apply.
  • Dispersed camping regulations apply when not in Dinkey Lakes Wilderness.

44585824.name: Coyote

44585825.description:
Statham Meadow Trail is 5.7 miles long that starts 0.7 miles down the Crown Valley Trail and is a good way to access Spanish Lakes, Geraldine Lakes, Cow Meadow, and Rodgers Creek. Early season the Rancheria Creek and Statham creek can be difficult and dangerous to cross. Also, there are many cow trails crossing the system trail so the visitors hiking or riding the trail must be diligent about staying on the Statham Meadow system trail. 

Spanish Trail is an OHV route that is 5 miles long and features Spanish Lake if one is willing to walk about a mile from the wilderness boundary where you park your OHV. Spanish OHV route which winds up a ridge to elevation of 9,000 feet overlooking Rough Spur, Spanish Mountain, and Garlic Meadow. 

Trail Map

description_map.need_to_know:
Statum/Spanish Area:

  • No campfires above 10,000 ft.
  • There are sit specific campfire restrictions in some of these areas.
  • Food and refuse must be stored in a container designed to prevent access by bears, or counter-balanced at least 15 feet above the ground and 10 feet horizontally from a tree trunk (where containers are not required).
  • John Muir Wilderness regulations apply.
  • Kings Canyon Wilderness regulations apply if entering the National Park.

44585825.name: Statham/Spanish

44585826.description:
Crown Valley is a popular hiking and horseback riding trail which starts at 6800 feet in elevation. Crown Valley Trail is 8.4 miles in length and is a great access point for Tehipite Valley Trail, Blue Canyon Trail, and Coyote Pass which is a cross country pass all which enter Kings Canyon National Park. Other destinations are Crown Rock, Castle Peak, and Chain Lakes accessible from the Crown Valley Trail. 

Rancheria Creek Trailhead starts at 7600 feet and is 3.8 miles and can also access the Crown Valley Trail on the 0.4-mile Rancheria Cutoff Trail. Recreational opportunities include Duck Lake 4.6 miles, and Chain Lakes 6.5 miles. For those who enjoy scenic vistas Hoffman Mountain and Castle Peak are nearby.

Crown/Rancheria Trails Map

description_map.need_to_know:
Crown/Rancheria Area:

  • John Muir Wilderness regulations apply.
  • Kings Canyon Wilderness regulations apply if entering the National Park.

44585826.name: Crown/Rancheria

44585827.description:
Woodchuck trail is a popular trail from Woodchuck Trailhead and is about an 18-mile loop, featuring a lake, and considered difficult due to the elevation gain and switchbacks. Woodchuck creek is about four miles and is your first major water source on the trail. The hike to Woodchuck lake is 11.2 miles. Also, Loper Peak is nearby at 10,045 feet, Crown Pass 10,188ft, and Halfmoon lake is 16.9 miles from the trailhead. 

Common Destinations: Woodchuck Creek, Woodchuck Lake, Crown Pass, Crown Lake, Chuck Pass. 

Woodchuck Trail Map

description_map.need_to_know:
Woodchuck Area:

  • No campfires above 10,000 ft.
  • Food and refuse must be stored in a container designed to prevent access by bears, or counter-balanced at least 15 feet above the ground and 10 feet horizontally from a tree trunk (where containers are not required).
  • John Muir Wilderness regulations apply.
  • Kings Canyon Wilderness regulations apply if entering the National Park.

44585827.name: Woodchuck

44585828.description:
The Maxson Trailhead provides access to the John Muir Wilderness and Kings Canyon National Park. It is a popular trail beginning at Courtright Reservoir at 8184 feet in elevation and leads to many scenic basins. The trail can access an adventurer to Red Mountain Basin, Bench Valley, or Blackcap Basin. The first major creek crossing is Post Corral Creek which is about 7 miles from Maxson Trailhead. In Red Mountain Basin Fleming Lake is 12 miles, Disappointment Lake is 14.5 miles, and Hell for Sure Pass at 11,286 feet is a 16-mile hike. Guest Lake in Bench Valley is 22 miles from the trailhead with Blackcap Mountain 11,559 feet nearby. The hike into Blackcap basin along the beautiful Kings River is 24 miles in length.  

Maxson Trail Map

description_map.need_to_know:
Maxon (Courtright) Area:

  • No campfires above 10,000 ft.
  • There are site specific campfire restrictions in some of these areas.
  • Food and refuse must be stored in a container designed to prevent access by bears, or counter-balanced at least 15 feet above the ground and 10 feet horizontally from a tree trunk (where containers are not required).
  • John Muir Wilderness regulations apply.
  • Kings Canyon Wilderness regulations apply if entering the National Park.

44585828.name: Maxson (Courtright)

44585829.description:
The Corbett Lake Trail starts at 7400 feet in elevation that follows Bolsillo Creek and ends at Corbett Lake which is at 9070 feet. The Corbett Lake Trail is 3.3 miles from the trailhead to the lake with 1,670 feet elevation gain. With cross country opportunities to Cunningham Lake and Givens Lake with Mount Givens in the background at 10648 feet. Great trail for day hikes, swimming, and fishing. 

Common Destinations: Bolsillo Creek, Corbett Lake, Givens Lake, Cunningham Lake, and Mount Givens. 

Corbett Trail Map

description_map.need_to_know:
Corbet Area:

  • No campfires above 10,000 ft.
  • Food and refuse must be stored in a container designed to prevent access by bears, or counter-balanced at least 15 feet above the ground and 10 feet horizontally from a tree trunk (where containers are not required).
  • John Muir Wilderness regulations apply.

44585829.name: Corbett

44585830.description:
Dutch/Crater Trailhead begins at Florence Lake by the day use parking and picnic area. The hike up to Dutch Lake Trail is 2.7 miles to Dutch lake gaining 1,785 feet in elevation to 9145 feet. The Dutch Lake trail continues another 2.4 miles to Dutch Oven Meadow and peters out a mile above Dutch Oven Meadow. The Crater Lake Trail is 3.9 miles up to Crater Lake at 9365 feet in elevation. These two trails are popular with equestrians and hikers alike above the beautiful Florence Lake. 

Common Destinations: Dutch Lake, Crater Creek, Crater Lake, Hidden Lake, Dutch Oven Meadow, and Summit Lake. 

Dutch/Crater Trail Map

description_map.need_to_know:
Dutch Area:

  • No campfires above 10,000 ft.
  • Food and refuse must be stored in a container designed to prevent access by bears, or counter-balanced at least 15 feet above the ground and 10 feet horizontally from a tree trunk (where containers are not required).
  • John Muir Wilderness regulations apply.

44585830.name: Dutch/Crater

44585831.description:
Florence Lake Trail gradually works its way around Florence Reservoir on exposed rocky outcrops. Look for birds of prey roosting in Jeffrey snags along the trail. Once on the south end of the reservoir, the trail crosses Boulder Creek and the South Fork of the San Joaquin. The San Joaquin has a bridge crossing but Boulder Creek may be difficult to cross in early season due to snowmelt. Little water is available on the first four miles of trail. The trail winds 4.3 miles around Florence Lake to the Ferry Trail junction. The distance to the popular Muir Trail Ranch and hot springs across the San Juaquin river is 9.5 miles. Sallie Keys Lakes are about a 14-mile hike and Seldon Pass at 10910 feet is a 15.8-mile journey. 

Florence Trail Map

description_map.need_to_know:
Florence Lake Trail Area:

  • No campfires above 10,000 ft.
  • There are site specific campfire restrictions in some of these areas. 
  • Food and refuse must be stored in a container designed to prevent access by bears, or counter-balanced at least 15 feet above the ground and 10 feet horizontally from a tree trunk (where containers are not required).
  • John Muir Wilderness regulations apply.
  • Sequoia and Kings Canyon wilderness regulations apply if entering the National Park. 
  • Special approval required for commercial use.

44585831.name: Florence

44585832.description:
The Hooper Trailhead is located 2.2 miles down the Hooper OHV Route before Jackass Campground. The dirt road is easy to negotiate and crosses a shallow section of San Joaquin River before arriving at the trailhead. The best way to locate the trail is find the wooden trailhead at the end of the dirt parking area. The Hooper trail is a faint foot trail which makes its way below Infant Buttes 10290 feet before crossing Hooper Creek and arriving at Harvey Lake in 5.5 miles. The terrain is steep and arduous, and the trail is faint, but the adventurer is awarded with great views in Hooper Basin. Gordon and Harvey are the first two lakes in the basin with Hooper, Neil, Foolish, Crazy, and Chamberlain Lakes nearby.

Hooper Trail Map

description_map.need_to_know:
Hooper Area:

  • No campfires above 10,000 ft.
  • Food and refuse must be stored in a container designed to prevent access by bears, or counter-balanced at least 15 feet above the ground and 10 feet horizontally from a tree trunk (where containers are not required).
  • John Muir Wilderness regulations apply.
  • Sequoia and Kings Canyon wilderness regulations apply if entering the National Park. 
  • Special approval required for commercial use.

44585832.name: Hooper

44585833.description:
Bear Diversion TH provides access to Bear Creek Trail and shares quota with Bear Cutoff. The trail follows the drainage of Bear Creek upstream from Bear Creek Diversion Dam. The trail is rated as strenuous as it gains much elevation working up and over granite outcrops along Bear Creek. The Bear Creek trail is 7.6 miles in length and gains 1,595 feet to the Pacific Crest Trail. The trail starts out in drier elevations and gradually enters wildflower filled meadows as it nears the Pacific Crest Trail. Water is plentiful as The trail return to the banks of Bear Creek repeatedly. Swimming in the creek can be dangerous in early summer due to snowmelt. This trail is NOT recommended for stock.

Bear Diversion Trail Map

description_map.need_to_know:
Bear Creek Trail Area:

  • This trail is not recommended for stock.
  • No campfires above 10,000 ft.
  • There are site specific campfire restrictions in some of these areas. 
  • Food and refuse must be stored in a container designed to prevent access by bears, or counter-balanced at least 15 feet above the ground and 10 feet horizontally from a tree trunk (where containers are not required).
  • John Muir Wilderness regulations apply. 
  • Special approval required for commercial use.

44585833.name: Bear Diversion

44585834.description:
Bear Ridge Trail follows the length of Bear Ridge 5.7 miles to access the Pacific Crest Trail at 9880 feet in elevation. The trail climbs steeply out of Lake Edison and quickly gains elevation, 2240 feet in 5.7 miles. A few miles from the trailhead, the trail passes through some of the most diverse forest in the region. Jeffrey Pine, Lodgepole Pine, Western White Pine, Junipers, and Firs can all be found growing in close proximity. The first few miles of trail can be notoriously dry. With usually one perennial stream about three miles from the trailhead. Nice hiking trail with great views of Edison Lake.  

Common Destinations: Pacific Crest Trail, Volcanic Knob 11140 feet, and Recess Peak 12813 feet. 

Bear Ridge Trail Map

description_map.need_to_know:
Bear Ridge Trail Area:

  • No campfires above 10,000 ft.
  • There are site specific campfire restrictions in some of these areas. 
  • Food and refuse must be stored in a container designed to prevent access by bears, or counter-balanced at least 15 feet above the ground and 10 feet horizontally from a tree trunk (where containers are not required).
  • John Muir Wilderness regulations apply. 
  • Special approval required for commercial use.

44585834.name: Bear Ridge

44585835.description:
Mono Creek Trailhead is in the parking area at just past the Vermillion Campground. It is located next to the Devils Bathtub trail head and meanders 4.8 miles around Lake Edison to the ferry landing. Mono Creek Trail leaves Edison Lake and heads east up the Mono Creek Drainage toward Mono Pass. Reaching Mono Pass can be quite strenuous as it is the highest on-trail pass in Sierra National Forest. It is 20.3 miles to Mono Pass which is 12075 feet in elevation. The trail continues 5.3 miles to Rock Creek on the Inyo National Forest. Many side drainages offer unique and solitary wilderness experiences. Water is plentiful as Mono Creek is fed by many tributaries.

Mono Creek Trail Map

description_map.need_to_know:
Mono Creek Area:

  • No campfires above 10,000 ft.
  • There are site specific campfire restrictions in some of these areas.
  • Food and refuse must be stored in a container designed to prevent access by bears, or counter-balanced at least 15 feet above the ground and 10 feet horizontally from a tree trunk (where containers are not required).
  • John Muir Wilderness regulations apply.
  • Special approval required for commercial use.

44585835.name: Mono Creek

44585836.description:
Devils Bathtub Trail makes for a great day hike or overnight trip for a novice party. The trail begins on the northwest shore of Edison Lake and climbs at a consistent grade to reach Devils Bathtub. The trail climbs 1400 feet in 4.5 miles. The Bathtub is a uniquely large montane lake perched under Graveyard Peak and the Silver Divide. Remember to camp 100ft from water while visiting Devils Bathtub.

Common Destinations: Devils Bathtub, Graveyard Lakes, Graveyard Peak 11494 feet, and Goodale Pass 10997 feet. 

Devils/Graveyard Trail Map

description_map.need_to_know:
Devils Bathtub Area:

  • No campfires above 10,000 ft.
  • There are site specific campfire restrictions in some of these areas.
  • Food and refuse must be stored in a container designed to prevent access by bears, or counter-balanced at least 15 feet above the ground and 10 feet horizontally from a tree trunk (where containers are not required).
  • John Muir Wilderness regulations apply. 
  • Special approval required for commercial use.

44585836.name: Devils/Graveyard

44585837.description:
Margaret Lakes Trail offers a rugged and solitary experience on the west end of the Silver Divide. The trail starts at the end of the Onion Springs OHV Route which is 4.7 miles long and requires high clearance four-wheel drive vehicles. The trail gains and crosses the Silver Divide on a dry and exposed ridgeline. The Margaret Lakes Trail is 9.9 miles and its 5 miles to Arch rock after climbing 2430 feet from the trailhead. After crossing the divide, hikers are rewarded by visiting one of the best granite arches in the United States: Arch Rock. The Trail continues down into the Margaret Lakes Basin and loops around to allow visitors to explore nearly every lake in this quiet basin.

Margaret Lakes Trail Map

description_map.need_to_know:
Margaret Lakes Area:

  • No campfires above 10,000 ft.
  • There are site specific campfire restrictions in some of these areas.
  • Food and refuse must be stored in a container designed to prevent access by bears, or counter-balanced at least 15 feet above the ground and 10 feet horizontally from a tree trunk (where containers are not required).
  • John Muir Wilderness regulations apply. 
  • Special approval required for commercial use.

44585837.name: Margaret Lakes

44585838.description:
The Sample Meadow Trail starts off Sample Meadow Road on Kaiser Pass. The Sample Meadow Trail is 3.4 miles and ends at Potter Pass at 8990 feet in elevation. Sample Meadow is a popular trail with good views and is 2.9 miles to Upper Twin Lake with an elevation gain of 516 feet. Lower Twin Lake and George Lake are also obtainable on the Kaiser Pass Loop. 

 Common destinations: Upper and Lower Twin Lakes, George Lake, Potter Pass, and Kaiser Peak at 10310 feet. 

Sample Meadow Trail Map

description_map.need_to_know:
Sample Meadow Area:

  • No campfires above 10,000 ft.
  • Food and refuse must be stored in a container designed to prevent access by bears, or counter-balanced at least 15 feet above the ground and 10 feet horizontally from a tree trunk (where containers are not required).
  • Kaiser Wilderness regulations apply.

44585838.name: Sample Meadow

44585839.description:
The Potter Pass trail out of Badger Flat is a popular hiking trail for day hikers as well as backpackers. The trail starts at 8300 feet before climbing 2.2 miles to Potter Pass at 8980 feet. The popular destination is Upper Twin Lake which is 4 miles. George Lake is 5.1 miles. The Potter Pass trail is a well-maintained trail with wonderful views of the Ansel Adams Wilderness at the top of Potter Pass.

Common destinations: Potter Pass, Lower Twin Lake, Upper Twin Lake, George Lake, and Kaiser Peak 10310 feet. 

Potter Pass Trail Map

description_map.need_to_know:
Potter Pass Area:

  • No campfires above 10,000 ft.
  • Food and refuse must be stored in a container designed to prevent access by bears, or counter-balanced at least 15 feet above the ground and 10 feet horizontally from a tree trunk (where containers are not required).
  • Kaiser Wilderness regulations apply.

44585839.name: Potter Pass

44585840.description:
Potter Pass Cutoff Trail is 2.2 miles and climbs 1160 feet to the top of Potter Pass 8980 feet. Potter Pass Cutoff trail is a good alternative to the busy Potter Pass Trail. Take time to enjoy the splendid views of the Ansel Adams Wilderness on top of Potter Pass. Upper Twin lake is the popular destination which is 4 miles. George lake is 5.1 miles.

Common destinations: Potter Pass, Lower Twin Lake, Upper Twin Lake, George Lake, and Kaiser Peak 10310 feet. 

Potter Cut-off Trail Map

description_map.need_to_know:
Potter Pass Cutoff Area:

  • No campfires above 10,000 ft.
  • Food and refuse must be stored in a container designed to prevent access by bears, or counter-balanced at least 15 feet above the ground and 10 feet horizontally from a tree trunk (where containers are not required).
  • Kaiser Wilderness regulations apply.

44585840.name: Potter Cut-off

44585841.description:
The Deer Creek Trailhead is located next to D&F Pack Station at Huntington Lake. The trailhead starts out at 7240 feet, and can access the Kaiser Loop Trail, College Rock Trail, and Potter Pass Cutoff Trail. The popular destination is taking the College Rock Trail 3.1 miles up to the beautiful College Rock with wonderful views of Huntington Lake. The College Rock trail climbs steeply from the Deer Creek Trailhead 1815 feet to the top of College Rock which is 9055 feet in elevation. From College Rock it is 2.6 miles to Kaiser Peak 10310 feet. The Kaiser loop is 14.4 miles and can be accessed from Deer Creek Trailhead or Billy Creek Trailhead. 

Deer Creek Trail Map

description_map.need_to_know:
Deer Creek Area:

  • No campfires above 10,000 ft.
  • Food and refuse must be stored in a container designed to prevent access by bears, or counter-balanced at least 15 feet above the ground and 10 feet horizontally from a tree trunk (where containers are not required).
  • Kaiser Wilderness regulations apply.

44585841.name: Deer Creek

44585842.description:
The Billy Creek Trailhead is located above Upper Billy Creek Campground at Huntington Lake. Billy Creek Trail is 2.3 miles long and intersects with the Mary’s Meadow Trail which is 1.9 miles in length. Billy Creek Trail also can access the Kaiser Loop trail and Coarsegrass Meadow Trail. The popular destination at Billy Creek Trailhead is to take the Kaiser Loop Trail 4.3 miles up to Nellie Lake. The trail is steep, and the elevation gain to Nellie Lake is 1920 feet, but the traveler will be rewarded with a wonderful hike.  

Common Destinations: Billy Creek, Mary’s Meadow, Nellie Lake, and Kaiser Peak 10310 feet. 

Billy Creek Trail Map

description_map.need_to_know:
Billy Creek Area:

  • No campfires above 10,000 ft.
  • Food and refuse must be stored in a container designed to prevent access by bears, or counter-balanced at least 15 feet above the ground and 10 feet horizontally from a tree trunk (where containers are not required).
  • Kaiser Wilderness regulations apply.

44585842.name: Billy Creek

44585843.description:
The Coarsegrass Meadow trail is 2.9 miles long and the trailhead is located at the end of Huntington Lake. The trailhead is off Huntington Lake road and does not have a trailhead sign. The trailhead is located on the last cove past Huntington Lake Resort on a small dirt turnout. This is a good trail for a hiker looking for some solitude in the Kaiser Wilderness. Coarsegrass Meadow Trail follows Home Camp Creek for 2.1 miles before crossing the creek and following the faint footpath about .5 miles to Coarsegrass Meadow. The traveler will enjoy a beautiful meadow setting with possible views of Jumpoff Point 8549 feet and Black Point at 8111 feet in elevation. 

Coarsegrass Meadow Trail Map

description_map.need_to_know:

44585844.description:
From Clovis: Take Highway 168 toward Shaver Lake. At the north end of Shaver Lake, turn north on Big Creek Road. Travel 6 miles, turn left on to Stump Springs Road. Travel 18 miles to Forest Road 7S26, turn right. Follow to Forest Road 7S78. Continue 1 mile on Forest Road 7S78 to trailhead.

Common Destinations: Westfall Creek, Gloria Meadow, and Hidden Lake.

44585845.description:
To get to the Pryor Lake Trailhead one can either take Sample Meadow Road to the 7S81 road or Stump Springs Road to the 7S81 road. The 7S81 one starts out as a rough dirt road and the last 1.5 miles of road 7S81 is classified as a four-wheel drive road with high clearance recommended. Take the 7S81 road to the very end where the Pryor Lake Trail Starts. Pryor Lake trail is 1.5 to 2 miles from the trailhead. The trailhead is at 7400 feet in elevation and Pryor Lake is at 8246 feet, so there is about 846 feet of elevation gain on this trail. Pryor Lake is quiet place in Kaiser Wilderness with an adventurous drive and wonderful opportunities for solitude.  

Common Destinations: Pryor Meadow, Pryor Lake, and Long Lake.
